title: The ¥20 Note Route: China's Li River, Stop by Stop | China Travel Expert
description:
The landscape printed on China's 20-yuan note is a real place — and you can sail right through it. Here's the route.

The Li River runs about 83 km from Guilin down to Yangshuo, threading between thousands of karst peaks. The exact scene on the ¥20 note is near Xingping — the "Yellow Cloth Shoal" reflections by Nine-Horse Fresco Hill — best reached by a small bamboo raft rather than the big cruise boat. Along the way, watch for cormorant fishermen, a 1,000-year tradition that's now fading and mostly kept alive for visitors. Drift on to Yangshuo's old West Street, then take your reward stop: a bowl of Guilin rice noodles (桂林米粉), a dish traced back over 2,000 years to Qin-dynasty soldiers.

🧭 Expert Tip: Do the raft at dawn — you get the river mist and beat the tour crowds, and the light on the peaks is at its softest.
